title: Physical Activity Guidelines for Adults
content:
Regular physical activity is one of the most important things adults can do for their health. The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Physical Activity Guidelines for Americans recommend:

For substantial health benefits, adults need at least 150–300 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic activity per week, or 75–150 minutes of vigorous-intensity aerobic activity, or an equivalent combination of both.

Moderate-intensity activities raise your heart rate and make you breathe faster but still allow conversation — examples include brisk walking, water aerobics, casual cycling, and doubles tennis.

Vigorous-intensity activities make you breathe hard and fast and make sustained conversation difficult — examples include running, swimming laps, singles tennis, and aerobics classes.

Adults should also do muscle-strengthening activities (such as weight training, resistance bands, bodyweight exercises, or heavy gardening) that work all major muscle groups on 2 or more days per week.

Moving more and sitting less at any level provides some health benefits. Even light-intensity activity — such as standing or slow walking — is better than being sedentary.

For adults who are inactive, starting with even 10–15 minutes of moderate walking per day and gradually increasing provides significant benefit. The key is progression: increasing frequency, intensity, or duration over time as fitness improves.

Children and adolescents aged 6–17 should do 60 minutes or more of moderate-to-vigorous activity every day, including aerobic, muscle-strengthening, and bone-strengthening activities.

People with chronic health conditions or physical limitations should be as physically active as their abilities allow and should discuss their specific situation with a healthcare provider before starting a new exercise programme.
source: Original — based on U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Physical Activity Guidelines for Americans, 2nd edition (federal publication, public domain)
